liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (4 reviews): Reviewer hears a funky, raw first outing of Shakedown Street, with strong vocals from Jerry; Reviewer calls this Shakedown Street incredibly good and among the tightest versions they have heard [9][10][13][18]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Going from Shakedown into Good Lovin', Bobby talks the audience through the transition; Reviewer finds the Good Lovin' less precise than the Shakedown before it [9][10]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 other sources): Not Fade Away contains a Nobody's Fault But Mine jam; The Not Fade Away includes a Nobody's Fault But Mine jam [1][2]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Opening Mississippi has strong harmonies on the 'grand-eo' line, followed by a nice long jam [12]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer says Peggy-O is not the best ever, but Jerry's vocals are great [12]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Bob drives a fiery Minglewood Blues, according to this reviewer [12]
- **From The Heart Of Me** (1 review): Reviewer says DeadBase 7 also lists this as the first From The Heart Of Me [13]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer notes Garcia snarling out some of the lyrics in Terrapin [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ollin Arageed**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 14 archived performances [20]
- Earliest performances in the archive: From The Heart Of Me [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-08-31.sbd.miller.125882.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 171 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1978-08-31.145138.nak301.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 177 min [2]
- **gd1978-08-31.158061.aud.hicks-fong.flac2448**: audience recording; 19 songs; 158 min [4]. Said about its sound: Half Step through Candyman is unlistenable; sound improved once the tapers moved closer; Some tracks begin abruptly because the deck was switched on late [4]
- **gd78-08-31.aud-sbd.miller.20726.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 155 min; rated 3.92/5 by 12 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says this matrix has good sound, and is the first Shakedown in such quality [13]
- **gd78-08-31.aud.wiley.11480.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 151 min; rated 3.14/5 by 7 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has an ugly cut in Terrapin just as the train pulls into the station, so the whistle is lost; Reviewer calls the audience recording a nice one [8][9]
- **gd1978-08-31.sbd-set2.wiley.11477.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 72 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [7]. Said about its sound: Moderate hiss in Ship Of Fools fades as the track goes on; Terrapin has a dropout at 7:39, with about 30 seconds removed [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first Red Rocks show; a carload from Yellowstone work arrived at 3 pm on showday, four of six new to the Dead [17]
- The audience tape captures the crowd reacting to the first live Shakedown Street, and they seem to enjoy it [18]
- Fans from the previous night's show said Stagger Lee had been played for the first time there [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-08-31.sbd.miller.125882.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Maxell UDXLI-C90) [1]. Also: Soundboard source with pitch correction, helped by Joe B. Jones; the encore comes from extra analog generations via Matt Smith [1]
- **gd1978-08-31.145138.nak301.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 301 mics (row 20, seats 77-80)(patched out of Barry Glassberg) > Sony TC-158SD (Maxell UDXLII) [2]. Also: T. Wiley's audience source patches Ship Of Fools, Samson, the first 4:29 of Terrapin, and short bits of Drums and Ollin Arageed [2]
- **gd1978-08-31.158061.aud.hicks-fong.flac2448**: taped by concert recording by John Hicks & Dennis Fong; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 09/2022; source: Handheld deck (mono) > Maxell-XLII [4]. Also: Audience recording possibly made on a portable Panasonic that John held at head level [4]
- **gd78-08-31.aud-sbd.miller.20726.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard and Audience composite [5]
- **gd78-08-31.aud.wiley.11480.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [6]
- **gd1978-08-31.sbd-set2.wiley.11477.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Tim Wiley; source: SBD>MR>DAT>CDR (?) [7]. Also: Second-set soundboard converted and seeded to Etree by T. Wiley in August 2002 [7]
